visual_blocks.preview: Tropical wet evergreen, semi-evergreen, moist deciduous, dry deciduous and thorn formations represent different ecological conditions; they are not canopy-density grades or legal protection ranks.

visual_blocks.heading: VISUAL FIRST

visual_blocks.heading: ANSWER-GRABBING OPENING - WRITE/ADAPT IN THE EXAM
visual_blocks.preview: Montane, sub-alpine and alpine vegetation reflect altitude and exposure in mountain systems; an elevational belt must not be presented as one nationwide legal forest category.

visual_blocks.preview: MONTANE SUB-ALPINE AND ALPINE ZONATION

visual_blocks.heading: CLOSING RECALL FLOW - FOUNDATION - MONTANE SUB-ALPINE AND ALPINE ZONATION

visual_blocks.heading: ANSWER-GRABBING OPENING - WRITE/ADAPT IN THE EXAM
visual_blocks.preview: Reserved Forest, Protected Forest and Village Forest arise through the Indian Forest Act framework, while unclassed forest is a record or administration expression; legal consequence must be checked from the applicable notification and law.

visual_blocks.heading: VISUAL FIRST
visual_blocks.preview: RESERVED PROTECTED VILLAGE AND UNCLASSED FORESTS

visual_blocks.heading: ANSWER-GRABBING OPENING - WRITE/ADAPT IN THE EXAM
visual_blocks.preview: The owner preserves the classic exam distinction: a Reserved Forest uses a more restrictive permission logic, whereas a Protected Forest does not create the same presumption; neither label is an ecological forest type.

visual_blocks.heading: VISUAL FIRST
visual_blocks.preview: RESERVED VERSUS PROTECTED PERMISSION LOGIC

visual_blocks.heading: CLOSING RECALL FLOW - CORE - RESERVED VERSUS PROTECTED PERMISSION LOGIC
visual_blocks.preview: START / CONCEPT: CORE — Reserved versus Protected permission logic

visual_blocks.heading: ANSWER-GRABBING OPENING - WRITE/ADAPT IN THE EXAM
visual_blocks.preview: Recorded forest area refers to land entered as forest in government records and may include different legal classes; degraded recorded forest can have little measured canopy, while measured cover can occur outside recorded forest.

visual_blocks.heading: VISUAL FIRST
visual_blocks.preview: FOREST COVER AND RECORDED FOREST AREA

visual_blocks.heading: ANSWER-GRABBING OPENING - WRITE/ADAPT IN THE EXAM
visual_blocks.preview: Tree cover is measured separately from forest cover under the applicable FSI methodology; combining them can describe canopy extent but cannot establish forest type, tenure or rights.

visual_blocks.preview: TREE COVER BOUNDARY

visual_blocks.heading: CLOSING RECALL FLOW - CORE - TREE COVER BOUNDARY

visual_blocks.heading: ANSWER-GRABBING OPENING - WRITE/ADAPT IN THE EXAM
visual_blocks.preview: The Forest Rights Act, 2006 is a rights-recognition and historical-injustice statute for forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes and eligible Other Traditional Forest Dwellers, not a blanket transfer of every forest to private ownership.

visual_blocks.heading: VISUAL FIRST
visual_blocks.preview: FRA HISTORICAL-INJUSTICE PURPOSE

visual_blocks.heading: CLOSING RECALL FLOW - CORE - FRA HISTORICAL-INJUSTICE PURPOSE
visual_blocks.preview: START / CONCEPT: CORE — FRA historical-injustice purpose

visual_blocks.heading: ANSWER-GRABBING OPENING - WRITE/ADAPT IN THE EXAM
visual_blocks.preview: The owner records occupation before 13 December 2005 and an additional three-generation or 75-year residence-and-dependence test for Other Traditional Forest Dwellers; Scheduled Tribe claimants do not face that OTFD generational test.

visual_blocks.heading: VISUAL FIRST
visual_blocks.preview: SCHEDULED TRIBE OTFD CUTOFF AND ELIGIBILITY

visual_blocks.heading: CLOSING RECALL FLOW - CORE - SCHEDULED TRIBE OTFD CUTOFF AND ELIGIBILITY
visual_blocks.preview: START / CONCEPT: CORE — Scheduled Tribe OTFD cutoff and eligibility

visual_blocks.heading: ANSWER-GRABBING OPENING - WRITE/ADAPT IN THE EXAM
visual_blocks.preview: An individual forest right concerns pre-existing habitation or self-cultivation under actual occupation, subject to the Act's conditions and statutory ceiling; recognition does not authorise fresh encroachment.

visual_blocks.heading: VISUAL FIRST
visual_blocks.preview: INDIVIDUAL FOREST RIGHTS

visual_blocks.heading: CLOSING RECALL FLOW - CORE - INDIVIDUAL FOREST RIGHTS
visual_blocks.preview: START / CONCEPT: CORE — Individual forest rights

visual_blocks.heading: ANSWER-GRABBING OPENING - WRITE/ADAPT IN THE EXAM
visual_blocks.preview: A community forest resource right is the community-level right to protect, regenerate, conserve and manage a traditionally used community forest resource; it is distinct from both IFR and the wider set of community-use rights.

visual_blocks.heading: VISUAL FIRST
visual_blocks.preview: COMMUNITY RIGHTS AND COMMUNITY FOREST RESOURCE RIGHTS

visual_blocks.heading: CLOSING RECALL FLOW - CORE - COMMUNITY RIGHTS AND COMMUNITY FOREST RESOURCE RIGHTS
visual_blocks.preview: START / CONCEPT: CORE — Community rights and community forest resource rights

visual_blocks.heading: ANSWER-GRABBING OPENING - WRITE/ADAPT IN THE EXAM
visual_blocks.preview: The Act also recognises habitat rights for Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups and pre-agricultural communities and traditional seasonal resource access where the statutory conditions are met.

visual_blocks.heading: VISUAL FIRST
visual_blocks.preview: HABITAT AND SPECIAL RIGHTS

visual_blocks.heading: CLOSING RECALL FLOW - CORE - HABITAT AND SPECIAL RIGHTS

visual_blocks.heading: ANSWER-GRABBING OPENING - WRITE/ADAPT IN THE EXAM
visual_blocks.preview: The claims route begins with the Gram Sabha and proceeds through Sub-Divisional and District Level Committees; filing or recommendation is not the same as final recognition, and recognition is not assumed without the completed procedure.
